newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty drifts sideways, may rise later, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Zloty drifts sideways, may rise later, depos ease.

text.p: The Polish zloty drifted just below the central bank firing line at 2.5 percent from parity in early trade, but dealers said it could tiptoe above it later today only to be punched down by a small-scale intervention.

On Wednesday the National Bank of Poland said it was satisfied with the zloty's exchange rate no stronger than at 2.5 percent from the trading band centre after five days of currency-buying interventions to keep the bullish zoty down.
"The zloty might even weaken slightly in early trade and then inch up to or past the intervention line at 2.5 percent and trigger NBP action," said Karol Zaluski of ING bank.

At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 2.48/2.45 percent from the parity rate, against 2.51/2.41 percent at opening. It was at 3.1490/00 against the dollar, down from 3.1460/95 at opening and 1.8320/25 against the mark, up from 1.8325/45.

"There might be some early zloty selling by banks' rebuilding currency positions cut on Wednesday, but there is a constant trickle of currencies onto the market from foreigners and exporters," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
"The zloty's move above the central bank set resistance is not likely to be a bold one and the ensuing possible intervention against it is likely to be cosmetic," he said.
Despite a net outflow of 406 million zlotys from the system on Thursday overnight rates on the money market traded at 19.70/19.90 percent, down from the opening 19.80/20.40 percent.
Tomorrow/next cash was also lower at 19.50/21.00 percent against 19.90/20.80 percent at opening but dealers expected both rates to rise later today on the back of NBP drainages.

The NBP offered to drain 1.4 billion zlotys through a 14-day reverse repo rate with a T/N value date and 300 million through a sale of 91-day NBP-bills with O/N value date. The reverse repo rate was last at 22.15 percent and the 91-day bill average yield was 22.19 percent.-Jan Strupczewski +4822653 9700
